title: Containment, Treatment Authority, Escalation and IPM Handoff

content.overview: Technician II can interpret trends and verify outcomes without gaining independent pesticide or regulated-treatment authority. Strong performance preserves quarantine and sanitation controls, identifies when the evidence exceeds role limits, and hands off a clear affected scope, trend, intervention history and next verification need.

vocabulary.definition: Role-specific authorization to select, mix, apply or direct a control under applicable law, label and facility procedures.
Defined control limiting movement from suspect or affected material/areas into clean production.
Reconstructable evidence supplied to the authorized role for a higher-consequence decision.

sections.title: Evidence does not create authorization
sections.body: A strong diagnosis or trend does not by itself authorize pesticide selection, mixing, application or another regulated treatment. Product legality, label requirements and facility authorization remain separate controls.

sections.title: Do not break containment to collect convenience data
sections.body: Sampling and follow-up must preserve quarantine, sanitation and clean-to-dirty workflow boundaries. If a needed action conflicts with containment, escalate the method rather than bypassing the boundary.

sections.title: Handoff should preserve both confidence and uncertainty
sections.body: State affected scope, sampling quality, trend, intervention history, outcome evidence, unresolved alternatives, containment status and the next decision required. Never rewrite prior observations to make the case look cleaner.

workedExamples: Trend evidence suggests failure of an authorized control, but a new pesticide is not selected by the technician; the case is escalated with the measured outcome and next-round recommendation.
A suspect propagation batch remains quarantined while confirmation is pending even though adjacent clean plants look normal.
commonMistakes: Treating diagnosis competence as applicator authority.
Moving suspect material to improve access for scouting.
Omitting negative or conflicting findings from the handoff.
content.practicalApplication: Produce an IPM follow-up report with sampling quality, annotated map, trend classification, intervention history, outcome evidence, biosecurity status, authority boundary, escalation trigger and next-round plan.
content.summary: Advanced IPM competence means defensible evidence, intact containment and clear escalation—not unauthorized treatment.

primaryVisuals.title: Containment, authority and IPM handoff
primaryVisuals.alt: Plant-health decision flow preserving quarantine, sanitation and clean-to-dirty movement controls, checking whether an action is within the technician's role and applicable product or facility authorization, and routing unresolved or regulated treatment decisions to an authorized role with an evidence-rich handoff.
primaryVisuals.caption: Strong diagnostic evidence does not create pesticide or regulated-treatment authority. Preserve containment, act only within authorization, and escalate with the measured scope, trend, intervention history and unresolved uncertainty.
